key_findings: 983 StreamingMatMul calls for 3 forward passes (3+1+1 tokens)
Only 197 unique tensors, but 983 calls = 786 repeated acquisitions
8971 MB of weight data dequantized — 4.4x the model file size (2019 MB)
74693 map calls (StreamingPin) — 75 per matmul on average
73728 incidental map calls — nearly 1:1 with map calls
100% of time attributed to compute (dequant+dot), 0% to acquisition
The 8971 MB read is 4.4x the model size, confirming massive redundant weight loading
conclusion: The dominant cost is repeated weight dequantization and mapping. Each forward pass re-acquires the same 197 tensors, reading 8971 MB total (4.4x model size). The 73728 incidental maps indicate the streaming window is too small for the tensor shards, forcing per-row remapping. Weight residency caching would eliminate the 786 repeated acquisitions and reduce bytes read from 8971 MB to ~2019 MB (model size).
next_step: B011: Implement weight residency cache in StreamingMatMul to eliminate repeated acquisitions
